mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising risk-free rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive during more than 50% of such contractions, or the mechanism fails when GDP contraction is accompanied by aggressive monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply-chain shock with high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over two months signals a housing demand boom decoupled from broader economic growth, which historically precedes equity market corrections within the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > +2% MoM and GDPC1 < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of monetary loosening.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS above 0.4% and a fall in UNRATE below 4% for two months signals a softening labor market after a period of tightness, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as cost pressures ease.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% and UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: transition from tight to loose labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present outside of non-recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate below 0.5% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% for more than six months and CPIAUCSL < 2.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation exceeds 3% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in RSAFS below -5% signals a sudden drop in household savings, which often coincides with increased consumer spending and short-term equity market gains over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high unemployment.
